prs.title: Route messages with a decision model
prs.status_label: Ready to open · waits for the keepup App
prs.founder_line: Your model router can pick a model with a small decision model instead of starting a full agent for each routed message, and today's agent stays as the fallback.
prs.why_it_fits: classifyWithLLM() starts a headless agent with the router's fallback model, and that agent's only job is to call select_category with one category from a fixed list. This is the job decision models were built for: one answer from a fixed list, with a probability for each option.
prs.risks: Routing moves to a different provider, so each classified message goes to OpenAI even when the router's fallback is another provider, and the answer is probabilistic. The setting is off by default. When it's on, classifyWithLLM() is unchanged and still answers when the chosen category's probability is under 0.70, when the call fails or is refused, when the API returns a category it wasn't offered, or when there is no OPEN_AI_KEY. A "none" at 0.70 or above is final and means no rule matched; a "none" under 0.70 goes to the agent, because a weak "none" can hide a rule that should have matched. From the 22 Oct update, a long category list is cached: a write costs 1.25 times normal input and lasts at least 30 minutes, so a router that gets less than about one message every 30 minutes can pay that rate on each message instead of getting a discount.
prs.rollback: Set ROUTER_CLASSIFIER=agent, or remove the setting.

stages.what_shipped: The Decisions API became generally available on 22 Oct, adding prompt caching on shared input, input_json and more questions per request.
stages.what_changes: Only server/utils/agents/aibitat/plugins/router-classifier.js and its test. A category list that looks long enough for the API's 1,024-token minimum moves into a shared prefix in input, with an explicit cache breakpoint before the user's message, because content in questions can't be cached. Length is judged from the list's size in bytes, so no tokenizer runs over the list, and a list near the minimum can land on either side of it, which only costs a missed discount. A shorter list keeps its plain choices with caching turned off, and gets no cache discount, and that includes the list in this fork's test set. Caching is turned off there because the API would otherwise write a long user message to the cache at the write rate. A cache write costs 1.25 times normal input and lasts at least 30 minutes, so a long list on a router that gets less than about one message every 30 minutes can pay that rate on each message instead of getting a discount. On a long list the descriptions leave the choices and the same 0.70 threshold applies, so it's a different request from the one the lab's table measures. The table only measures the short form, and the lab's separate long-list check, once it has run, covers the test set's rules padded with neutral text, with its messages sent back to back, so its cache reads are the best case and a router with a long list should check its own labelled examples before relying on this. input_json isn't used: the message is plain text, and JSON parts can't carry a breakpoint. The default stays agent.

A "none" at 0.70 or above is final and means no rule matched; a "none" under 0.70 goes to the agent.

prs.title: Keep audio uploads working after 26 Feb 2027
prs.status_label: Ready to open · waits for the keepup App
prs.founder_line: Audio uploads that use OpenAI would stop working on 26 Feb 2027, when OpenAI shuts down the model they use, so this moves them to its replacement and makes the model something you can change in settings.
prs.why_it_fits: collector/utils/WhisperProviders/OpenAiWhisper.js sets this.model = "whisper-1", so after 26 Feb 2027 audio uploads that use the OpenAI provider will fail. gpt-transcribe is OpenAI's recommended model for completed recordings, which is what these uploads are.
prs.risks: A different output shape or price. The provider reads only the text field of OpenAI's answer, and the lab checks the response fields and both prices. OpenAI warns that changing the model doesn't keep every capability, such as word timestamps and subtitles; this provider uses neither. The lab's recordings run one to two minutes, so it says nothing about long files: OpenAI's guide states a 25 MB limit and no length limit. The lab sends only mp3, so the .ogg, .oga and .opus uploads the collector accepts are untested on gpt-transcribe: OpenAI's guide and its API reference disagree on ogg, and neither lists oga or opus. If OpenAI refuses the configured model, the upload fails with an error that names the model and the setting. Not covered here, and each needs its own change before 26 Feb 2027: voice input defaults to whisper-1, through its own setting, at server/utils/SpeechToText/openAi/index.js:8 and frontend/src/components/SpeechToText/OpenAiOptions/index.jsx:76, and the fallback list at server/utils/helpers/customModels.js:306 offers whisper-1 when the live model list call fails, along with gpt-4o-transcribe and gpt-4o-mini-transcribe, which shut down the same day.
prs.rollback: Set the Transcription Model setting (WHISPER_OPEN_AI_MODEL) back to whisper-1, which works until 26 Feb 2027.

vendor.claim: whisper-1 shuts down on 26 Feb 2027, and the recommended replacements are gpt-live-transcribe or gpt-transcribe

lab.note: Running this lab sends each LibriVox recording through the fork's OpenAI provider with whisper-1 and with gpt-transcribe, then records word error rate against the published text, time to the result and the listed price per minute; it needs OPENAI_API_KEY.

prs.title: EmbeddingGemma 2 for the native embedder · recall@5 0.848 → 0.950 on a 1,000-passage SciFact subset
prs.status_label: Ready to open · waits for the keepup App
prs.founder_line: Your built-in document search can use a newer on-device model that reads many languages, and your current model stays the default.
prs.why_it_fits: Native search defaults to all-MiniLM-L6-v2 (trained on English, capped at 512 tokens), but chunks here stop at 1,000 characters, so the limit rarely bites. The case is languages and the library: EmbeddingGemma 2 covers 100+ languages, and @xenova/transformers has had no release since 29 May 2024.
prs.risks:
Switching to or from this model clears all embeddings and removes every document from every workspace, and nothing re-embeds on its own. People have to add their documents again. That holds in either direction, as for any embedder model change. The settings page already warns and asks first, and the model's description repeats it. Its vectors have 768 dimensions, against 384 for MiniLM.

A small server can run out of memory. This entry caps chunks at 2,000 characters, because a batch of longer chunks ran a 3.5 GB container out of memory. The cap doesn't make it small. At the cap, one batch of 5 peaked at 2,202 MB on Chinese text against 773 MB on English (evidence/memory-probe.log). That is more than the 2 GB machine the embedder's own comment says it was benchmarked on. Chinese is the only such language we measured.

This tokenizer has no effective length limit: its config says 1e+30. So a chat message is cut to its first 2,000 characters before it is embedded for search, and the chat keeps the whole message. A longer message is searched on its opening only. Without that cut, one message ran the same container out of memory at 60,000 characters of English and at 16,000 of Chinese (evidence/query-cap-before.log). With it, both finished, peaking at 470 MB and 807 MB (evidence/query-cap-after.log). The developer API's embeddings route isn't capped: behind an API key, it passes its input straight to the embedder.

EmbeddingGemma 2 is opt-in, but the library move is not opt-in for any existing model. all-MiniLM-L6-v2, nomic-embed-text-v1 and multilingual-e5-small all load through the new package, with the same quantized files, dimensions and token ids. MiniLM stays the default, but its vectors move slightly, for queries as well as documents. Within either package, batching alone moves them further than that. So existing workspaces keep working without being identical, and the lab's notes show what that does to MiniLM's search. nomic-embed-text-v1 moves further: the lowest cosine between packages is 0.986 on 50 SciFact passages and 0.977 on 25 claims. What that does to its search has not been measured. People on that model search old document vectors with new query vectors until they add their documents again. multilingual-e5-small's vectors did not move, to six decimal places. All of this was measured on @huggingface/transformers 4.3.2 on linux/arm64 only.

The download is bigger: the 4-bit text model is 175 MB, against 23 MB for MiniLM. Embedding is slower on small machines. The model is not on AnythingLLM's download mirror, which answers 404 for it, so it downloads only from Hugging Face. If the server can't reach Hugging Face when someone picks it, their documents have already been cleared, because the reset runs first. The failed download is then logged and the server stays up. Documents can't be embedded until Hugging Face is reachable, when the next attempt loads it with no restart. Before this guard, the same choice with Hugging Face blocked ended the server process (evidence/hf-unreachable-before-fix/crash.json).

The installed server grows because onnxruntime-node ships its binaries for every platform. On linux/x64 its install step would also download CUDA files from NuGet, about 260 MB that the CPU embedder never uses. It would also fail the whole install if NuGet can't be reached. server/.yarnrc skips that step, which we tested on linux/amd64 under emulation with NuGet blocked. sharp 0.35, which the new package asks for, requires Node 20.9, so it's pinned to 0.34.5 under that package. Node 18 installs keep working, and only image features the embedder doesn't use depend on it.
prs.rollback: Picking all-MiniLM-L6-v2 again in the embedder settings clears embeddings and removes documents again, so people add their documents back to re-embed them; the code can be reverted without touching the reranker or local Whisper.

table.notes:
Test set: the first 200 BEIR SciFact test queries by id, against a 1,000-passage SciFact subset: every passage relevant to those queries (198), plus the 802 lowest-id other passages, out of 5,183 in the corpus, with brute-force cosine search through the pull request's NativeEmbedder.

Recall on a subset isn't comparable to published SciFact scores, which search the whole corpus.

Each passage was embedded whole, with no text splitter, for both models, so these scores compare the models on whole passages and are not the chunked path the product uses. 847 of 1,000 passages are longer than the 1,000 characters the product cuts all-MiniLM-L6-v2 at, and 157 of 1,000 are longer than the 2,000 it cuts EmbeddingGemma 2 (q4) at.

Machine: one Docker container on Node v18.20.8, arm64, 8 CPUs, @huggingface/transformers 4.3.2. Each model ran in its own process.

Same default: all-MiniLM-L6-v2 scores recall@5 0.848 on the old package and 0.848 on the new one, and 0.848 when documents embedded on the old package meet queries embedded on the new one. Both give 384 dimensions. On 200 passages cut to the 1000 characters the product sends, the lowest cosine between packages is 0.994420; on whole passages it is 0.996092.

Batching: on the same 200 chunks of all-MiniLM-L6-v2, the lowest cosine between packages is, one at a time 0.995903, in batches of 25 0.994420. Within one package, alone against batched: old 0.989910, new 0.992124. The same batches twice on the new package: 1.000000. 200 queries one at a time, between packages: 0.992230. Token ids differ between packages on 0 of 400 of these texts.

The other existing models also move to the new package, and were loaded for real on both. Xenova/nomic-embed-text-v1: lowest cosine between packages 0.985660 on 50 chunks, 0.976709 on 25 queries, 768 dimensions on both, token ids differ on 0 of 75 texts. MintplexLabs/multilingual-e5-small: lowest cosine between packages 1.000000 on 50 chunks, 1.000000 on 25 queries, 384 dimensions on both, token ids differ on 0 of 75 texts.

prs.founder_line: Anyone who runs your Claude examples as written gets an error instead of an answer, or soon will, because they name models Anthropic has retired or is about to retire.
prs.why_it_fits: examples/minimal/anthropic.toml:14 uses claude-sonnet-4-20250514. Anthropic has retired it, so requests return an error. This is the minimal Anthropic example. examples/complete/reasoning-models.toml is AURA's example for Claude's thinking settings, so its model and those settings have to stay valid.
prs.risks: Only example TOML files change: no Rust, no defaults, and nothing a running deployment reads unless it copied these files. The new models think by default, so these examples spend output tokens on thinking that AURA doesn't show. rig's Anthropic parser has no case for a redacted_thinking block, which Anthropic says the API might return when thinking is on, so such a reply would reach the user as an error; an example can't guard against that, and the fix belongs in the rig fork. On a worker that calls tools, rig's stream parser also discards a thinking block with empty text, signature included (rig/rig-core/src/providers/anthropic/streaming.rs:393 at the rev this base pins, and the same check at 097d08d), and these models return their blocks empty by default. So rig drops the empty thinking block from the worker's next request, against Anthropic's rule to pass thinking blocks back unchanged in tool-use loops, including empty ones, and the worker's follow-up turns lose its reasoning until the rig fork round-trips empty blocks with their signatures. Anthropic says adaptive thinking doesn't need a turn to start with a thinking block, and that the API might disable thinking when the history is incompatible, so this may never show up as an error. An example can't guard against this either. Older Claude ids stay as they are where they use another provider or are commented out: examples/minimal/bedrock.toml:21, examples/minimal/openrouter.toml:22, examples/reference.toml:226, 235 and 249, examples/quickstart-orchestration-math/config.toml:46, .env.example:21 and deployment/helm/aura/values.yaml:119. That's every id outside crates/ at the base commit. Under crates/ they're in tests and one doc comment, plus the CLI's curated list at crates/aura-cli/src/init/provider.rs:85, and none of those change. examples/minimal/openrouter.toml:22 is live, not commented out, and names anthropic/claude-sonnet-4, which OpenRouter no longer lists (its model list, read on 1 Nov 2026), so that example is left for a follow-up.

prs.founder_line: People using AnythingLLM can pick OpenAI's newest models and chat with them, even when the app can't fetch OpenAI's live model list.
prs.why_it_fits: AnythingLLM's fallback list only matters when its call to OpenAI's live model list fails, and at this commit it has nothing newer than gpt-4o. Its OpenAI provider also sends a temperature on every chat, which OpenAI's GPT-6 guide says to remove at the default reasoning effort.
prs.risks: The list doesn't check access, so a key without these models gets OpenAI's own error when chatting, as with every other entry. With temperature left out, a workspace's temperature setting has no effect on GPT-6 models; older models keep what they send today, and a test pins that. AnythingLLM reads context windows from LiteLLM's published list, not from this file, so until an install's cached copy lists a new model it treats the model as 4,096 tokens and compresses long prompts to fit, against the 1,050,000 on OpenAI's model pages. Any new OpenAI model behaves that way at this commit and this change doesn't alter it; LiteLLM's list had all three models when checked on 1 Nov 2026.
prs.rollback: Revert this pull request's commits: they add list entries and one temperature rule, and change no settings or stored data.

prs.title: Your default OpenAI model shuts down on 23 Oct · move to gpt-5.6-luna
prs.status_label: Ready to open · waits for the keepup App
prs.founder_line: Chats with no model set stop working on 23 Oct, and this moves the default to OpenAI's named substitute.
prs.why_it_fits: With no model set, AnythingLLM falls back to gpt-4.1-nano: server/models/systemSettings.js:878 for settings, server/utils/AiProviders/openAi/index.js:24 for chats, and server/utils/agents/index.js:318 and :857 and server/utils/agents/ephemeral.js:516 for agents. OpenAI shuts that model down on 23 Oct and names gpt-5.6-luna, released on 9 Jul, as its substitute.
prs.risks: Nothing a person chose changes, which cuts both ways: the settings screen stores whichever model is selected when it's saved, so anyone with gpt-4.1-nano in OPEN_MODEL_PREF or on a workspace stays on it and still stops working on 23 Oct. Anyone with no model set moves to a different model: OpenAI's pricing page lists gpt-5.6-luna at $0.20 input and $1.20 output per million tokens, against $0.10 and $0.40 for gpt-4.1-nano, and the provider's existing rule for gpt-5 models sends it a temperature of 1 whatever the workspace sets. AnythingLLM reads context windows from LiteLLM's published list, so until an install's cached copy lists gpt-5.6-luna it treats the model as 4,096 tokens and compresses long prompts to fit; the list had it at 922,000 tokens when checked on 1 Nov 2026.
prs.rollback: Set OPEN_MODEL_PREF back to gpt-4.1-nano, or revert this commit. Either only holds until 23 Oct: that model no longer answers after that.
